analysis.title: When Opposites Stop Attracting
key_insights: S&P 500 is down over 1% but S&P breadth is positive (+128). This is the 67th day this year that price and breadth moved in opposite directions, 33% of all trading days and the most in any calendar year back to 1996 with more than two months remaining.
The constant rotation has kept an 80%+ NYSE downside volume day from occurring in nearly a year and has insulated the SPX from a material drawdown since March.
Mechanism: when AI stocks rise, yields rise and breadth suffers. When AI stocks fall, yields fall, which helps breadth.
BTIG expects the rotation to stop at some point and a higher-correlation selloff to follow. It says this has been elusive, but correlations should rise unless 'it's different this time'.

The AI complex is the only group that is oversold, and BTIG calls it 'bad oversold' because it cannot bounce off key support. It contrasts this with 'good oversold' in rate-sensitive names over the last few weeks.

Groups that rallied on lower rates (homebuilders ITB, REITs IYR, utilities XLU) are no longer oversold and are meeting initial resistance. BTIG says they are not shorts, but the long trade gets harder.

Homebuilders bounced in line with the historical median 20-day gain of +6.44% from similar set-ups. ITB is at its 50-day moving average and BTIG would begin reducing tactical exposure. It could still push to its 200-day at 96.48.

Healthcare (XLV) is extended and looks vulnerable. BTIG had thought an XLV pullback could benefit XBI, but expected rising correlations make that hard to play near-term. Staples (XLP) are also extended into resistance.
Energy trades poorly despite WTI crude up about 2% on the day. OIH is down about 5% on the day and 18% from its highs.
Refiners look priced for perfection. Valero (VLO, Not Rated) is starting to break a very steep uptrend in place since June.
